`expect.stringMatching("...")` reads the string as a regular expression, as in Jest and Vitest. Before Bun 1.5 it looked for a substring. A text like `"total (net)"` no longer matches itself.

The rule skips strings that look like patterns: an anchor, a backslash, `|`, `.*` or a range like `[a-z]`.

`--fix` renames the call in files that import from `bun:test`. In other files it's a suggestion.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/prefer-string-containing" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { expect } from "bun:test";

expect(invoice).toEqual({ label: expect.stringMatching("total (net)") });
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect } from "bun:test";

expect(invoice).toEqual({ label: expect.stringContaining("total (net)") });
expect(invoice).toEqual({ id: expect.stringMatching("^inv_") });
expect(invoice).toEqual({ id: expect.stringMatching(/^inv_/) });
```
